title: Inside Your Ear
description: To hear the faint chime of a hidden bell fragment, you must understand your own amazing sound detector — the ear.

content.value: The ear is a natural instrument that catches vibrations from the air and turns them into signals your brain understands as sound. It has three parts: the outer ear, the middle ear, and the inner ear.

PINNA      → the outer flap that collects sound
EAR CANAL  → tube that carries sound inward
EARDRUM    → thin stretched membrane that vibrates
MIDDLE EAR → tiny bones that amplify the vibration
INNER EAR  → converts vibration into nerve signals
AUDITORY NERVE → carries the signal to the brain

The most important part is the EARDRUM — a thin, tightly stretched skin like a tiny drum. When sound waves reach it, it vibrates back and forth. These vibrations are passed on and eventually sent to the brain as the sounds we recognise.
The eardrum is delicate! Never poke anything sharp into your ear — a damaged eardrum can seriously harm your hearing. Very loud sounds can hurt it too.
Key Takeaway: The ear collects sound with the pinna, funnels it to the vibrating eardrum, and the inner ear turns those vibrations into signals sent to the brain by the auditory nerve.

quiz.question: Which part of the ear vibrates when sound reaches it?
quiz.explain: The eardrum is a thin stretched membrane that vibrates when sound waves hit it.

quiz.question: The outer flap of the ear that collects sound is the…
quiz.explain: The pinna is the visible outer flap that gathers sound and directs it into the ear canal.

quiz.question: The signal from the ear is carried to the brain by the…
quiz.explain: The auditory nerve carries the sound signal from the inner ear to the brain.
